page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.metal-12xl is a bare-metal general-purpose compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R05 processor operating at clock speeds up to 5.0 GHz across 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core without hyperthreading. The processor integrates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory comprises 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 running at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Network connectivity features a dedicated 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth, optimized for high-throughput data movement and Elastic Block Store integration. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or discrete hardware GPU accelerators. Hardware security and virtualization primitives include AMD Secure Virtual Machine (SVM), Indirect Branch Restricted Speculation (IBRS), and Speculative Store Bypass Disable (SSBD), delivering bare-metal isolation without hypervisor overhead.

Benchmark results place the system in the top tier for raw execution and memory throughput. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 3,156.0 and a multi-core score of 32,996.0, coupled with a multi-core stress-ng metric of 201,425.18. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 530.58 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth reaches 200.67 GB/sec. Data processing capability is reflected in Redis SET throughput measuring 178.57 million operations per second and static web throughput exceeding 120 GB/sec. For CPU-based machine learning inference, prompt processing reaches 7,012.51 tokens per second on lightweight models.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the bare-metal profile eliminates virtualization jitter while delivering high performance per core through dedicated physical allocations and DDR5 memory. The absence of bundled local storage requires complete reliance on network-attached storage architectures, representing an architectural tradeoff for disk-heavy pipelines. The platform is well suited for demanding workloads such as software compilation, distributed databases, low-latency in-memory data structures, network routing services, and high-frequency web applications.
